title: TIE/ln fighter (Star Wars)
intro: The TIE fighter is a fictional starfighter of the Galactic Empire in the Star Wars films: a ball-shaped cockpit between two flat wing panels, with twin ion engines, no shields and no hyperdrive. The pilot wears a sealed pressure suit and helmet and holds a two-grip yoke, with the targeting screen in front and the big round window ahead.

areas.name: Octagonal forward viewport
areas.text: The big framed window at the front of the ball.

panels.name: Octagonal forward viewport
panels.text: The large eight-sided window at the front of the ball cockpit.
panels.context: The pilot looks and aims through it; there is no canopy as in other fighters.

controls.name: Octagonal window
controls.text: A big window with a segmented frame, like spokes of a wheel. The pilot sights the enemy through it.
controls.context: It is the TIE fighter's main view; the targeting screen below helps with aiming.

controls.name: Top hatch
controls.text: A hatch above the seat. Pilots climb in from above.
controls.context: TIE fighters hang in racks in their hangars, so the pilot enters through the top.

areas.name: Targeting display
areas.text: The screen in front of the yoke.

panels.name: Targeting display
panels.text: A screen in front of the yoke that helps the pilot aim.
panels.context: It shows the target and when it is locked.

controls.name: Targeting screen
controls.text: A screen with a green crosshair and pictures of the target.
controls.context: The pilot lines up the target in the crosshair before firing.

controls.name: Range and lock readout
controls.text: Numbers and marks beside the target picture show the distance and whether the target is locked.
controls.context: A locked target is the moment to fire.

areas.name: Side panels
areas.text: Switch panels on the curved walls of the ball.

panels.name: Side panels
panels.text: Switches, lights and the radio on the curved walls beside the seat.
panels.context: The film shows them without naming each switch.

controls.name: Switch rows
controls.text: Rows of toggles and lights on the left and right of the TIE pilot's seat.
controls.context: They belong to the fighter's systems; the film does not show what each does.

controls.name: Comms
controls.text: The radio link to the squadron and to the station.
controls.context: TIE pilots fly in groups and get their orders over the radio.

areas.name: Rear viewport
areas.text: The small window behind the pilot.

panels.name: Rear viewport
panels.text: A small window in the back of the ball cockpit.
panels.context: It gives a little view behind the fighter.

controls.name: Rear window
controls.text: A small round window in the back of the ball cockpit.
controls.context: It lets light in and gives a glimpse behind; enemies behind are hard to see in a TIE.

areas.name: Control yoke and throttle
areas.text: The hand controls the pilot flies with.

panels.name: Control yoke
panels.text: The yoke with two hand grips in front of the pilot.
panels.context: The fire buttons sit under the thumbs.

controls.name: Control yoke
controls.text: Pushing the yoke forward or pulling it back tips the nose down or up; turning it rolls and turns the fighter.
controls.context: The pilot holds it with both hands, one on each grip.

controls.name: Fire buttons
controls.text: Buttons on the yoke grips under the thumbs fire the two laser cannons under the cockpit.
controls.context: The TIE has no shields, so it relies on speed and numbers; its guns fire straight ahead.

panels.name: Throttle
panels.text: This stands for the control that sets the craft's speed.
panels.context: The film does not show this control clearly; the catalog adds it so a joystick set has a place for the speed.

controls.name: Throttle (not clearly shown)
controls.text: This axis stands for the craft's speed: forward for faster, back for slower. The screen does not show where the real control sits, so its place is a guess.
controls.context: On a stick and throttle set this is the throttle lever; in the work itself the pilot is mostly seen with both hands on the flight controls.
